name: voidrancho
description: The database layer for Void Core applications: runes and mantles stored, indexed, queried and paged at scale, with edge weights as first-class floats, clustering, and a matrix view of a mantle that learned world models can read. One layer above Core, like Void Palabra and Void Maiz; Core stays pure.
status_note: 0.1.0 (2026-10-30): rungs 1-5 built and tested — Void Hormiga's store extracted and generalized (round trip, query parity with ls --tag, weights/ports/provenance/typed columns, format-1 migration), the write path with Hormiga's model-based test, the working set and Leiden clustering with weights, the matrix view with sparse algebra and a .npy training export, the network-path open policy, and snapshots as content-named segments. Void Hormiga's library builds on it (2026-11-02; its 2 GB exit test passed), and graph analysis (voidrancho_graph, a leaf target) moved here from Void Maiz the same day.
kind_note: A library with no user-facing install, hence `runtime`; the schema has no `library` kind.

requires.name: voidcore
requires.note: Linked for four things, all at its C ABI: vc_tag_match (every query is decided by Core's own evaluator, as SPEC 5 requires), the SPEC 6.1 codec (vc_arg_quote, vc_argv_split_json), and a manager for VcCore (the default CoreLink). The floor is 0.2.14 because measure runes, `kinds` annotations and declared glyphs in state.glyphs are what the typed columns, V and clustering read; query parity is tested against 0.2.15's tags/tag.c. Rancho is never linked BY Core.

interacts_with.name: voidcore
interacts_with.note: Rancho stores and indexes Core state documents and keeps them in step after each dispatch through a CoreLink (rancho/core.hpp); every change still enters through Core's dispatcher. Its one standing ask of Core is `touched` on the journal (Core's world models phase 1), which would make write-back exact instead of reading the command.

interacts_with.name: voidhormiga
interacts_with.note: First client. Rancho's Store, WorkingSet, Plan and JsonStream keep the API of Hormiga's src/store with the same meanings; a format-1 store Hormiga wrote is migrated in place on open. Adopted 2026-11-02: Hormiga's library keeps no copy of the store, and its .miga v4 bundle is written on this API (vacuum_into, purge, put_blob; remove_blob and clear_blobs at its ask).

interacts_with.name: voidmaiz
interacts_with.note: Not linked by Rancho. Graph analysis moved from Maiz to Rancho on 2026-11-02 (the author's ruling): Maiz's voidmaiz_graph target bridges to voidrancho_graph by including cmake/voidrancho_graph.cmake, so its names and its standing alone are a contract. Maiz ships the CoreLink adapter for its Core (maiz::RanchoLink).

interacts_with.name: voidsquid
interacts_with.note: Planned second client: its assets.db copies Hormiga's schema. Per-tag provenance (the source column) is its finding that tags launder.

interacts_with.name: voidpalabra
interacts_with.note: Not linked. Segments are named by SHA-256, Palabra's content hash, so identical bytes have one name across the family. The line between Palabra's persistence and Rancho's store is still to agree (okf/design/open-questions.md §2).

interacts_with.name: voidbicho
interacts_with.note: Planned. The .npy export of the matrix view is the first form of the training data Bicho's world-model experiment would read; embeddings Bicho computes are to be stored beside it, keyed by spirit id and provenance.

interacts_with.name: voidmago
interacts_with.note: Reads this manifest to build the family compatibility matrix.

documents.store: a SQLite file (format 2): Hormiga's tables plus edge weights/ports, tag sources, the row index, typed fields, cluster settings, blobs
documents.matrix_view: a directory of NumPy .npy arrays and manifest.json (format voidrancho.matrix-view/1)

provides.effects_note: None registered with Core: every read or write of a store is I/O, done by the host's call into Rancho, never through Core's effect seam.

platforms_note: Built and tested on windows-x64 (MSYS2 ucrt64, GCC 15). The Linux and macOS paths (media detection by statfs) are written and not yet built.
